newsitem.title: UK: UK SIB to publish financial regulation paper Thurs.
newsitem.headline: UK SIB to publish financial regulation paper Thurs.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said it will publish on Thursday its broad plan setting out the new regulatory structure for the financial services industry which has been dubbed Super-SIB.
The paper, produced for Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, is the product of a project team set up by the SIB.

It includes representatives from the current regulators -- SIB, the Bank of England; Personal Investment Authority (PIA); Securities and Futures Authority (SFA); and the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
The team was given the brief of setting out a broad framework for the reform of the regulatory structure which will replace the current four regulators with one authority.
It has looked at proposals for the transition to the new authority and its structure, taking into account the views of investors and practitioners.
Since the team was set up, the government has announced that Super-SIB will also regulate Building Societies and supervise the Insurance industry.
The project team was assisted by consultants from McKinsey and Co and Kinsley Lord.

The SIB has said it will consult widely in the autumn and noted that the new Financial Services Bill would not be published in draft form until next year, allowing for a further period of consultation before it is considered by Parliament.

The SIB will hold a briefing for the press on Thursday at 1400 GMT, chaired by its outgoing head Sir Andrew Large who is to be replaced by current deputy governor of the Bank of England Howard Davies.
